ed-hall-charlotte-1905-08-01.A1:
BRUTE HUNTED DOWN
Woman's Cries Brought Help in Her Hour of Peril.
Ed. Hall, a young negro, made a desperate attempt to commit a criminal assault upon Mrs. Mack Auten, the young wife of a farmer, at her home four miles southeast of the city this morning. Hall afterward made his escape, and with a hundred men on his trail eluded capture until 4 o'clock this afternoon, when he was arrested at Pineville, this county, and safely landed in jail here. There was some talk of lynching this morning but this has quieted down and the authorities apprehend no trouble.

The outrage was committed at about 9:30 o'clock. The negro, who is employed in the city as a driver at Auten's meat market, was sent to Auten's home after some meat. He was half drunk. Upon some slight pretext he went into the house and asked Mrs. Auten to phone to town for him. As she complied and was turned with her face to the phone, the negro threw his arms around her from behind and attempted to drag her into an adjoining room.

The woman screamed loudly and put forth efforts to free herself, but the negro did not desist in his criminal purposes. Mrs. Auten continued her cries for help and was heard by a Mr. Beatty, who was working near by. As Beatty started toward the house the negro broke and ran. Mrs. Auten was found on the floor, half fainting. Her clothes were badly torn and an examination showed several bruises on her arm and body. When Mrs. Auten was revived she told graphically of the assault and gave a good description of the negro.—Charlotte Special to Raleigh Post.
ed-hall-charlotte-1905-08-01.A2:
Negro Attempts Rape in Charlotte.
Charlotte, July 26.—Ed. Hall, a young negro attempted criminal assault upon Mrs. Mack Auten, at the home of her husband, four miles east of the city on the Dilworth road, this morning, but was foiled in his purpose. The outrage was committed about 9:30 o'clock. The negro, who is employed in the city as driver at Austin's meat market, was sent to Auten's home after some meat. He was half drunk. Upon some slight pretext, he went into the house and asked Mrs. Auten to 'phone to town for him. As she complied and turned her face to the 'phone, the negro threw his arms around her from behind and attempted to drag her into an adjoining room.

The woman screamed loudly and put fourth efforts to free herself, but the negro did not desist in his criminal purpose. Mrs. Auten continued her cries for help and was heard by a Mr. Beatty, who was working nearby. As Mr. Beatty started toward the house the negro broke and ran. Mrs. Auten was found on the floor in a fainting condition. Her clothes were badly torn, and an examination showed several bruises on her arm and body. Where the negro had clutched her arm there was a great red ring. Hall was captured this afternoon at Pineville, N. C.
ed-hall-charlotte-1905-08-01.A3:
A SEVEN YEAR SENTENCE.
Ed Hall Receives It for Attempted Assault on Mrs. Mack Auten.
(Special to News and Observer.)
Charlotte, N. C. Aug. 17 — Ed. Ha

(Special to News and Observer.)

Charlotte, N. C., Aug. 17.—Ed Hall. the negro who attempted a criminal assault on Mrs. Mack Auten, was this afternoon sentenced to seven years in the penitentiary. The case occupied about ten minutes. Just time enough for Mrs. Auten to give her testimony and Judge Osborne to submit. It did not go to the jury. Judge Cook sentenced Hall to seven years in the penitentiary, saying that the limit of the law and that on account of the negros age he believed that would be the just punishment.

will-horn-hattiesburg-1905-08-17.A1:
AGED MAN SHOT
BY A CONVICT
By Associated Press.
jieshurg Miss Aug 4
Hattiesburg, Miss., Aug. 4.—J. G. Smith, an aged white man in charge of the city convict force was shot and killed to-day by William Horn one of the negroes in the gang. The murderer escaped to adjacent woods where one hundred men have him surrounded.
will-horn-hattiesburg-1905-08-17.A2:
KILL GUARD; LYNCHED.
Two Negro Convicts Hanged to Bridge for Murder.
Hattiesburg, Miss., Aug. 4.—J. G. Smith, city convict guard, was assassinated this morning by two negroes of his gang, William Horn and "Kid" George. Horn escaped, but George was captured, together with Ed Lewis, alias Brock, who struck the shackles from the murderers. They were put in the city jail after Brock had been futilely whipped to force him to tell where Horn had gone. To-night a mob quietly took the two negroes from jail and hanged them to a bridge in the glare of an electric light.

will-horn-hattiesburg-1905-08-17.A11:
FORTY SOLDIERS PREVENT LYNCHING OF NEGRO BY MOB Detail of Mississippi Militia Brings Depersonal Implicated in Assassination to State Capital. REPUBLIC SPECIAL Jackson, Miss., Aug. 17.—A detail of forty soldiers, under command of Adjutant General Fridge and Major Virgil Jones, arrived in Jackson at 8 o'clock to night, having in custody Will Horn, the negro desperado who assassinated J. G. Smith, a city prison guard at Hattiesburg, several days ago. Horn was saved from mob violence by Governor Vardaman's action in sending troops from Gulfport to the rescue. A movement was on foot at Hattiesburg to organize a mob and lynch the negro immediately after his arrival there, but no attempt was made when the train pulled into Hattiesburg with the car windows bristling with Krag-Jorgensen rifles. When the special train arrived in Jackson it was met at the depot by Governor Vardaman, who thanked the soldiers for their work. The negro was turned over to Sheriff Spann of Hinda County, and transferred to jail. He makes a full confession and implicates four other prisoners, in addition to the two negroes who were lynched at Hattiesburg on the night of the assassination.

Menefee, who, it is said, represented himself to be a buyer for the New Roads Hardware Company of New Roads, La., was arrested yesterday at the Jefferson Hotel, on complaint of the Charter Oak Stove and Range Company, and the Simmons Hardware Company, which firms allege that they cashed worthless drafts for him.

It is also said that Menefee is wanted in Chattanooga, Tenn., where he is said to have lived there to the Chattanooga Wagon Company, and in Monroe, Mo., where he is alleged to have secured money under false pretenses.

According to the story told to the police by the Simmons Hardware Company Menefee induced the concern to cash a draft for $100 July 15. This draft was later discovered to be worthless, it is alleged.

August 5 he is alleged to have visited the Charter Oak concern, where, as a buyer for the Louisiana hardware store, he purchased a bill of goods amounting to $20. He then had a draft for $100 cashed, it is charged. The concern says the draft was worthless.

Menefee was arrested by Detectives Labarge and McCarthy. He is a prisoner at the Central District Station. Menefee has been stopping at the Jefferson during his sojourn in St. Louis. He denies the several charges made against him.

will-horn-hattiesburg-1905-08-17.A12:
TRYING TO HEAD
OFF JUDGE LYNCH
Governor Vardaman Calls Out Troops to Protect Negro From Wrath of Mob.
JACKSON, MISS. Aug. 17.—Governor Vardaman was informed by telegraph this afternoon that a negro named Horn, had been captured between Lumberton and Hattiesburg and that he was in charge of Sheriff Moody and a posse. The negro was charged with complicity in the killing of Convict Guard Smith near Hattiesburg, last week, for which two negroes were lynched.

Governor Vardaman was also informed that a mob was being formed at Hattiesburg to lynch Horn. He at once ordered Adjutant General Fridge at Gulfport to take a detail of troops to take charge of Horne and bring him to Jackson for safe keeping.

General Fridge at once started on a special train to relieve Sheriff Moody who was hiding the negro in the woods.
will-horn-hattiesburg-1905-08-17.A13:
Innocent Men Were Lynched.
Will Horn, one of the negroes who killed Street Commissioner Smith at Hattiesburg August 4, and for which crime two negroes were lynched the next day, was landed in jail at Jackson, Miss., by Adjutant General Frigid and a military company, called out by Governor Vardaman to protect Horn from lynching. Horn admits the killing freely but says he never intended to kill. He states further that one of the negroes lynched by the mob was innocent.
will-horn-hattiesburg-1905-08-17.A16: There are now three negroes confined in the jail at Jackson for the murder of Mississippi officials. They are Will McPhay, for killing a special officer at Summit; Ollie Williams, for the murder of Constable Joe Boyd, and Will Horn, who led the murderous assault on the street commissioner of Hattiesburg. Horn's companions in this crime were caught shortly after and lynched. Horn was captured in the southern part of the State a few days ago and was escorted to Jackson by the Lumberton military company.—Daily Clarion-Ledger.
